caption:
Threat actor advertises subscription MaaS RAT for Windows combining remote access, credential theft, silent Chromium extension deployment, memory execution, and persistence via tasks, registry, and LNK files. Delivery via VBS/JS/SVG/LNK/HTA. Anti-VM and obfuscation included.

alt_text: A threat actor advertises a subscription MaaS RAT with a silent Chromium extension and memory execution. Dark cinematic scene of an abstract Windows malware package under stress.

ThreatMon reported a bundled MaaS offering that combines a RAT, credential theft, and silent browser extension deployment under subscription billing. Abstract before-and-after pattern of subscription malware packaging.

The offering bundles remote access, credential theft, anti-VM techniques, memory execution, and multiple persistence methods that support long-term access. High-contrast motif of a Windows system under stealth compromise.

The package uses DLL injection, process hollowing, sleep obfuscation, and a silent Chromium extension for credential theft while persisting through scheduled tasks. Clean abstract diagram of its capabilities.

Many organizations lack visibility into silent browser extension deployments and memory-only execution, so file-based scanning misses the loader. Dark scene of an overlooked extension audit checkpoint beside an ignored checklist.

Audit Chromium extension policies, block silent sideloading, and monitor for anomalous scheduled tasks and memory injection. Calm orderly workflow of extension policy verification and permission gates.

Subscription MaaS now bundles a RAT, credential theft, and silent browser extension abuse with memory execution, so the barrier for operators keeps dropping. Minimal high-contrast malware-package symbol in deep negative space.

sources.supports: Original advertisement post describing the subscription MaaS offering, target platforms, capabilities (RAT, credential theft, silent Chromium extension, anti-VM, memory execution, obfuscation, injection, persistence), and delivery vectors.

Independent corroboration that the pattern is real and current. Kaspersky (April 2026) documents a subscription-tier MaaS RAT with an auto-builder, anti-analysis, and credential theft from Chromium-based browsers. It does not confirm this specific advertised product.
